title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for intent→configuration artifacts produced by a declared model (gpt-5-mini). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, provenance-grounded run accounting, a concise diagnostic explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and precise pointers into the archived execution bundle for independent verification.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for intent-driven network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, policy-driven changes, and automated remediation. Operational trustworthiness of such agentic pipelines depends strongly on external deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution to detect and mitigate incorrect, unsafe, or noncompliant outputs. Prior work emphasizes generate→validate→repair patterns and prototype emulation, but quantitative cross-vendor estimates of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation over a strong static validator are scarce. We therefore preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that asks the following research question: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are (1) a full preregistered paired experimental design anchored to a machine-verifiable preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e), (2) an artifact-grounded confirmatory execution over 720 paired tasks with exact statistical reporting, (3) an evidence-based explanation for the negligible aggregate guarded benefit in this regime, and (4) compact reproducibility pointers to the archived execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system reports describe architectures and safety patterns for LLM-assisted NetOps and AIOps, recommending workflow-centred mitigations including static validators, formal verifiers, and sandboxed execution to reduce operational risk. Prototype tools and transfers from program-verification domains show that emulation or symbolic analysis can expose runtime failures missed by static checks in some settings, while empirical studies of LLM-assisted code/specification generation show both hallucinations and improvements arising from external verifiers. These prior findings motivate our paired, workflow-level measurement (validator-only versus validator+emulation) rather than a model-ranking exercise. Closest conceptual precedents combine generation with validation and emulation in limited-scope NetOps prototypes, but none provide a preregistered, paired coverage matrix across misconfiguration classes with archived run accounting as we provide here.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a machine-readable plan (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) prior to execution. Design: paired-binary under shared_initial_candidate semantics. For each task a single sampled initial candidate (shared) was produced and reused by both the baseline and guarded analyses; thus, any between-condition discordance could arise only from (i) guarded-stage emulation observations that reveal a violation not detected by the static validator, or (ii) a permitted repair-stage invocation recorded in run accounting. Planned confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples; preregistered minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 (20 percentage points). Power planning targeted ≈80% power under conservative baseline-rate assumptions.

Task bank, vendors, and inclusion. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. The task bank abstracts three vendor-CLI families (labels vendor A/B/C used as CLI families) and a small set of topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance per the preregistered rules; parser failures were handled deterministically with up to two automatic reseeds. In the confirmatory execution no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred and complete_pair_count = 720 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model, sampling semantics, and orchestration. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and max_output_tokens = 2000. The recorded temperature field is null in the model_configuration artifact; explicitly, null indicates no explicit temperature parameter was supplied in the request and must not be interpreted as sampling determinism (temperature=0). The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: one sampled initial candidate per pair was reused by both baseline and guarded condition assessments and recorded in per-episode archives (per-episode shared-initial response files). Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full intent-constraint checks (syntax, workflow ordering, required-field presence, policy constraints). Guarded: baseline validator followed by a sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate against the emulated topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. Repair policy: at most one repair-stage model call per task (per preregistered contract; recovery calls are recorded in the provider-call audit).

Analysis plan and implementation. Primary analysis executed via paired_binary_analysis_v1 (preregistered executor). We report an exact McNemar two-sided test and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI using 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Primary analysis used complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were preregistered as exploratory with Bonferroni-adjusted intervals; these exploratory artifacts are archived but not expanded in-text because the confirmatory aggregate effect is near-zero.
sections.results:
Execution summary and run accounting. Confirmatory execution completed: planned_episode_count = 1440, completed_episode_count = 1440, failed_episode_count = 0 (execution/execution_manifest.json summary). Model calls used = 721 (recorded as hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 in provider_call_audit); stage accounting: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. No cross-condition cache reuse was observed (cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 721).

Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). Analysis artifacts report: baseline_success_count = 719, guarded_success_count = 720; baseline_success_rate = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded_success_rate = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These statistics are reported exactly as produced by paired_binary_analysis_v1 and archived in analysis/results.json.

Discordant-pair provenance pointer and repair attribution. The single discordant (n10 = 1) arises either from a guarded-stage emulation observation outside static-check coverage or from the single recorded repair-stage invocation. For independent verification we provide an artifact-grounded pointer: open the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl (file SHA-256 = df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) and search for the unique record where baseline_score == 0 and guarded_score == 1; that record contains the discordant pair_id and its per-episode validator and emulation traces. The single repair-stage invocation and provider-call accounting that align with that pair are recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha256 = 49731a2e52e049ccf5b53c35ddac2351ad75e7e95504dc4a42bcb096d0dec3aa) and in the execution manifest provider_call_audit (hosted_model_call_event_count = 721; stage_counts.repair = 1). Reviewers can use these three archived artifacts together (execution/raw_results.jsonl; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; execution/execution_manifest.json) to identify the exact pair_id and to confirm that the single repair-stage call maps to the n10 discordant outcome.

Representative diagnostics and validator coverage. Representative per-episode artifacts (artifact_examples and execution/responses for task-000001..task-000006) show validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, validator_version = 5.0, violation_count = 0 for the vast majority of curated items, and normalized_configuration outputs matching expected intent sequences. The archived validation_before/validation_after traces in per-episode scoring artifacts demonstrate that most candidates satisfied the validator's rule set; this explains the baseline ceiling (0.9986) and the absence of many discordant cases.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy and deterministic reseed handling were followed; missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 720 and zero failed episodes. No deviations affecting the primary estimand are recorded in the archived deviation log. Contamination checks reported zero flagged items for the confirmatory execution (analysis/contamination_summary.csv).
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregated benefit negligible? The artifact-backed evidence supports three proximate explanations. (1) Validator ceiling effect: the deterministic validator provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and workflow misconfigurations encoded in the synthetic task bank; baseline success_rate ≈ 0.9986 leaves little headroom for guarded-stage discovery. (2) Task curation: confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies but not adversarially crafted to evade known static rules; this concentrates tasks inside the validator's coverage envelope. (3) Paired/shared_initial semantics and accounting: identical initial candidates across conditions mean between-condition differences are constrained to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls; provider-call audit records a single repair-stage call consistent with the single n10 discordant count.

Operational interpretation and boundary conditions. Our finding implies that when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs conform to that validator's expected patterns, sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at the aggregated level. This narrow conclusion should not be generalized: in production regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial mutations, stateful multi-step interactions, or validator gaps (unknown vendor behaviors), guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation can yield substantive additional detections. The archived per-episode traces illustrate agreement between validator and emulation in this curated corpus and identify the single discordant episode for inspection.

Statistical and design sensitivity. The study was preregistered to detect a minimum paired difference of 0.20 (20 percentage points) with ≈80% power. The observed discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Thus, this execution yields a well-powered near-zero aggregate finding for the specific experimental regime rather than evidence that guarded stages never provide value.

Reproducibility and archived verification. We archived all per-episode raw results, validator and emulation traces, the execution manifest, and analysis artifacts. Key artifact pointers (with recorded SHA-256 digests) are: execution/raw_results.jsonl (df367ecc40a6...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (efe6e8e7...), analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (49731a2e...), execution/model_configuration.json (a40e96e2...), and provenance/master_prompt.txt (1872df1e...). Independent verification steps are documented in the repository manifest: (1) locate the unique baseline_score==0 & guarded_score==1 record in execution/raw_results.jsonl to obtain pair_id and per-episode traces; (2) confirm provider-call accounting and the single repair-stage invocation via analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and the execution manifest; (3) reproduce the paired analysis from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.

Recommendations for follow-up work. To expose regimes where guarded stages add meaningful marginal detection value we recommend (a) constructing adversarial and noisy task banks that intentionally exercise validator blind spots, (b) evaluating multiple validator families and higher-fidelity emulators across diverse vendor-CLI behaviors, and (c) relaxing shared_initial_candidate semantics in controlled experiments to measure interactions between generation variability and guarded-stage efficacy.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping (execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design and recommend targeted follow-up experiments on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, multiple validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are discussed in the execution manifest and provider_call_audit artifacts.
